According to the latest issue of the Power On newsletter, Apple is said to have once considered introducing a feature for Apple Upgrade that would make setting up a new iPhone almost seamless: Apple would pre-transfer your data for you. However, this feature ultimately never came to fruition.

The concept is simple: if users upgrade their devices on a fixed monthly payment plan at regular intervals, why not make the transfer process as easy as possible? Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman reports as follows:

There are clearly some loopholes in this. First of all, your iCloud backup will be slightly outdated, because data transfer can only take place when the device is shipped, which will be a few days behind the actual date, unless you choose to pick it up in-store.

In addition, there are obvious privacy concerns. If you use iCloud backup, it shouldn't come as a surprise that Apple holds your data. But for the general public, they may be concerned about how the data is transferred to the new phone, and may also question whether anyone has peeked at it during the process.

Two years ago, Apple launched a new system called "Presto" in its retail stores, allowing employees to update devices while the iPhone is still in the box. It is conceivable that this system could be extended in the future to support iCloud backup transfers, without anyone needing to view your data throughout the process.

That said, the feature ultimately never launched, which might actually be a good thing.
